original_question: Do the geodetic systems of Diophantine equations associated with K4, the Petersen graph, and the Hoffman-Singleton graph share a hidden common structure in the distribution of their variables that would make it possible to construct the corresponding system for generating every geodetic graph homeomorphic to the still-undiscovered Moore graph with k = 57, including that graph itself?
target_in_paper: Section B, item 3 under "Open Problems Related to Construction and Enumeration": whether a common hidden structure in the variable distributions of the geodetic systems of Diophantine equations for K4, the Petersen graph, and the Hoffman-Singleton graph could be used to construct the analogous system for the undiscovered Moore graph with k = 57, including that graph itself. ([dizzw.com](https://dizzw.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/Deutsche-internationale-Zeitschrift-f%C3%BCr-zeitgen%C3%B6ssische-Wissenschaft-%E2%84%9636-2022.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s exact target: it correctly identifies the three base graphs (K4, Petersen, Hoffman-Singleton), the focus on a hidden common structure in the distribution of variables of their geodetic Diophantine systems, and the intended application to constructing the system that generates all geodetic graphs homeomorphic to the undiscovered Moore graph with k = 57, including the graph itself. ([dizzw.com](https://dizzw.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/Deutsche-internationale-Zeitschrift-f%C3%BCr-zeitgen%C3%B6ssische-Wissenschaft-%E2%84%9636-2022.pdf))
missing_details: The paper places Section B under an explicit standing assumption: these construction/enumeration problems are asked assuming that the characterization conjectures stated in Section A are true. That hypothesis is implicit in your draft and should be stated. ([dizzw.com](https://dizzw.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/Deutsche-internationale-Zeitschrift-f%C3%BCr-zeitgen%C3%B6ssische-Wissenschaft-%E2%84%9636-2022.pdf))

The note defines "homeomorphic" in the subdivision sense: two graphs are homeomorphic iff both can be obtained by insertion of vertices onto edges, and each graph is homeomorphic to itself. This is needed for a stand-alone formulation. ([dizzw.com](https://dizzw.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/Deutsche-internationale-Zeitschrift-f%C3%BCr-zeitgen%C3%B6ssische-Wissenschaft-%E2%84%9636-2022.pdf))

The target graph is not just any Moore graph with k = 57; in the paper it is the still-undiscovered diameter-2 Moore graph arising as the remaining open case after the 5-cycle, Petersen graph, and Hoffman-Singleton graph. ([dizzw.com](https://dizzw.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/Deutsche-internationale-Zeitschrift-f%C3%BCr-zeitgen%C3%B6ssische-Wissenschaft-%E2%84%9636-2022.pdf))

The Section B setup implicitly restricts the technique to geodetic blocks for which the associated geodetic system of Diophantine equations is constructed, with each vertex of the given block having degree k >= 3. That scope is not stated in your draft. ([dizzw.com](https://dizzw.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/Deutsche-internationale-Zeitschrift-f%C3%BCr-zeitgen%C3%B6ssische-Wissenschaft-%E2%84%9636-2022.pdf))

The present note does not restate the explicit equations, variable indexing, or full formal definition of each geodetic system; it only refers back to the construction technique from [6]. So the sharpest paper-faithful rewrite should keep the paper’s terminology rather than inventing a more explicit algebraic specification not given in this note. ([dizzw.com](https://dizzw.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/Deutsche-internationale-Zeitschrift-f%C3%BCr-zeitgen%C3%B6ssische-Wissenschaft-%E2%84%9636-2022.pdf))
refined_question: Assuming the characterization conjectures stated in Section A, does there exist a common hidden structure in the distribution of the variables of the geodetic systems of Diophantine equations associated with K4, the Petersen graph, and the Hoffman-Singleton graph that would allow one to construct the geodetic system of Diophantine equations generating every geodetic graph homeomorphic, by edge subdivision, to the still-undiscovered diameter-2 Moore graph of degree 57, including that Moore graph itself? ([dizzw.com](https://dizzw.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/Deutsche-internationale-Zeitschrift-f%C3%BCr-zeitgen%C3%B6ssische-Wissenschaft-%E2%84%9636-2022.pdf))
justification: The draft is essentially a near-paraphrase of Section B, item 3, rather than any neighboring problem: the distinctive combination of "hidden structure," "distribution of the variables," the three named graphs, and the degree-57 Moore graph appears together only there. The immediately preceding definitions supply the meanings of "homeomorphic" and "Moore graph," while the Section B preamble makes the dependence on the earlier characterization conjectures explicit. The paper does not provide an explicit equivalent reformulation of this item. ([dizzw.com](https://dizzw.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/Deutsche-internationale-Zeitschrift-f%C3%BCr-zeitgen%C3%B6ssische-Wissenschaft-%E2%84%9636-2022.pdf))
